title: Vibe coded by non-technical dev, demo on Steam
author: Jason9mm
selftext:
I can't write a line of code, but I have background in game dev (publishing, design). I now have a https://store.steampowered.com/app/4948880/Type\_the\_World\_Demo/.

The game is a chill typing game where you write names of places on a world map. There's a keyboard on screen with ghost hand overlays that show the player which finger to use with each key. You can asses the quality by checking out the demo, I think it's ok.

So I used Claude Code Pro plan (about 24 € per month), Godot 4.7 and Superpowers skill plugin. A friend made the graphics, sounds and music are from Pixabay. I started this in April, but worked on a hobbyist-like schedule.

This was mainly a proof of concept project for me. As I don't indeed know how to code at all, I wanted to see if I can put together a game. It turns out I can.

Technically, Claude retrieves the world map vector data from public domain Natural Earth. The rest is pretty general. I (well, Claude) localised the game in seven languages, with additional name checking from GeoNames.

The Superpowers plugin is really helpful, I can't imagine not using something similar. Still Claude did make some spaghetti code decisions which had to be refactored later, but since Claude was able to do that as well, it was just a bit of extra time and token cost. It's pretty funny how working with Claude wasn't completely different than with a human programmer on Slack or whatever (you know, a fully motivated, always available, very nice, pretty darn quick, skilled but not infallible one).

Overall I'm freaking impressed! One can now just make games (of limited scope and quality) even with literally no coding skill. And with minimal cost. And it's super interesting and fun! Like yeah the indie games market will turn even more difficult but then again this can be a worthwile hobby for other than coders as well. I'm definitely going to make another, a more personally meaningful game now that I have seen that I can.
